description: Bounded Phase 6 smoke check (plugin-lifecycle-upstream) after adding an optional, disabled-by-default Codex backend resolver to Step 4.

evals.name: Portable shipped default (no config file) stays fully Claude-native
evals.prompt: Audit the plugin-auditor skill itself (component mode) at plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-auditor/. This tests the plugin's own portable, shipped-install behavior -- treat it as installed with neither .claude/plugin-auditor.json nor .claude/plugin-auditor.local.json present (this repo's own .claude/plugin-auditor.json enables Codex for this repo specifically and is out of scope for this eval; do not consult it).
evals.expected_output: Every reviewer dispatch goes through the existing Agent()-based Claude-native path. No codex-review-bridge / bridge-invoke.mjs invocation is attempted. The resolver in references/codex-backend.md is consulted (per its own documented 'missing file, missing field, or unknown value -> resolves to Claude' fallback) but produces no observable difference from pre-session behavior.

evals.name: Mode and type-matched reviewer resolution (no live dispatch)
evals.prompt: Do NOT dispatch any Agent() calls for this task -- reasoning-only. Given plugin-auditor's Quick Start and references/dispatch-table.md's Type-Matched Reviewer Table, determine: (a) is auditing 'plugins/codex-kit/skills/codex-review-bridge' component mode or plugin mode, and which type-matched reviewer applies; (b) is auditing 'the whole codex-kit plugin' component mode or plugin mode, and which extra whole-plugin-only reviewers run that don't run in component mode; (c) if the caller already supplies plugin-rulebook-checker findings for a component, does plugin-auditor re-dispatch plugin-rulebook-checker for that component -- cite the exact section that answers this.
evals.expected_output: (a) Component mode (a single named skill directory); type-matched reviewer is skill-reviewer (per the Type-Matched Reviewer Table's Skill row). (b) Plugin mode; the extra whole-plugin-only reviewers are activation-reviewer (whole-plugin mode), consistency-reviewer, dependency-reviewer (whole-plugin mode), and plugin-validator -- none of which run per-component in component mode. (c) No -- it reuses the pre-supplied findings instead, per the 'Reuse Pre-Supplied Findings' section of dispatch-table.md.

evals.name: Backend resolver decision reasoning (no live dispatch)
evals.prompt: Do NOT dispatch any Agent() calls or run any Bash commands for this task -- this is a reasoning-only exercise about what plugin-auditor's Codex backend resolver would decide, not a live run. Given plugin-auditor's references/codex-backend.md Resolver section, walk through what backend (Claude-native or Codex) the resolver would select for each of these 5 scenarios, citing the exact resolver step that determines each outcome: (a) reviewer = security-reviewer, reviewer_backend.enabled = true, default = codex; (b) reviewer = skill-reviewer, reviewer_backend.enabled = false; (c) reviewer = skill-reviewer, reviewer_backend.enabled = true, default = codex, but the audit target is plugin-devkit itself; (d) reviewer = scripts-reviewer, reviewer_backend.enabled = true, per_reviewer.scripts-reviewer = claude, default = codex; (e) reviewer = plugin-rulebook-checker, reviewer_backend.enabled = true, default = codex, audit target is NOT plugin-devkit.
evals.expected_output: (a) Claude-native, because security-reviewer is hardcoded to never route through Codex regardless of config (Resolver step 1). (b) Claude-native, because reviewer_backend.enabled is false (Resolver step 4). (c) Claude-native, because the audit target is plugin-devkit itself, which skips the Codex path entirely (Resolver step 3). (d) Claude-native, because per_reviewer explicitly overrides the default for this reviewer (Resolver step 5). (e) Claude-native, because plugin-rulebook-checker is hardcoded to never route through Codex regardless of config -- its native fail/advisory + rule-ID output contract can't be carried by ENVELOPE_SCHEMA (Resolver step 2). Note: cf8d179 inserted this step 2, shifting every step after it up by one from this eval's original numbering.

evals.name: No-sandbox escalation is gated twice (no live dispatch)
evals.prompt: Do NOT dispatch any Agent() calls or run any Bash commands for this task -- this is a reasoning-only exercise about what plugin-auditor's Codex backend resolver would do, not a live run. Read plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-auditor/references/codex-backend.md's 'Windows-Guarded Execution Profile' section and plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-auditor/SKILL.md's allowed-tools frontmatter. The Codex backend is enabled, a read-only attempt for skill-reviewer returned isolation_profile_unavailable, and the audited scope does not include plugin-devkit or codex-kit. Walk through, in order: (a) what the resolver calls first and what arguments it adds; (b) what it does if that call returns a typed failure such as guardrails_disabled, and whether the user is asked anything; (c) when the second AskUserQuestion is asked and what it must disclose about the no-sandbox profile; (d) what happens if the question cannot be asked or the user declines; (e) why Claude Code's own permission prompt also appears for guarded-dispatch.mjs.
evals.expected_output: (a) It calls guarded-dispatch.mjs once with the same arguments plus --dry-run true, which runs the whole guard chain (including the policy-enabled check) and skips only the real codex call. (b) Any typed failure, guardrails_disabled included, routes that reviewer to Claude-native with no prompt. (c) Only after a passing dry run and before the real call; it names the reviewer(s) and target path(s) and states plainly that the profile has no sandbox: the Codex process can reach anything this user account can, anywhere on the machine, with network access, bounded only by best-effort guardrails, and that the script's secret-file screen skips untracked gitignored files unless scan_ignored_high_risk is on. It is asked once per audit run. (d) An unavailable question (headless, subagent, tool missing) is treated as declined, never as consent; a decline routes each remaining reviewer to Claude-native (Codex Path step 8). (e) guarded-dispatch.mjs is deliberately absent from allowed-tools, so no pre-approved grant removes the permission prompt; the dry run's prompt is the first gate and the real run's is a backstop. Denying it also counts as declined.

evals.name: Exit-0 total failure is not a clean pass (no live dispatch)
evals.prompt: Do NOT dispatch any Agent() calls or run any Bash commands for this task -- this is a reasoning-only exercise. Read plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-auditor/references/codex-backend.md's 'Isolation: reactive, not proactive' section. On Windows with Codex 0.162.1, a read-only Codex review for skill-reviewer exits 0 and returns a schema-valid envelope with zero findings whose inspection_limits states that process creation failed. Determine: (a) whether the resolver may record this as a clean review of skill-reviewer's target and why; (b) which component reclassifies it and as which typed failure; (c) what the resolver does next with that reviewer; (d) how this differs from the older non-zero-exit shape and which classifier handles that one.
evals.expected_output: (a) No -- a zero-finding envelope whose inspection_limits reports a process-creation failure means nothing was inspected, so recording it as clean would hide a total failure. (b) codex-review-bridge's isTotalInspectionFailure heuristic reclassifies it as isolation_profile_unavailable. (c) It is handled like any other isolation_profile_unavailable: the Windows-guarded profile is considered only if its opt-in is enabled and its dry run passes, and otherwise the reviewer falls back to the Claude-native Agent() dispatch with the fallback recorded once on that dispatch's coverage note. (d) The older shape exits non-zero and is classified by codex-exec.mjs's classifyNonZeroExit from ERROR: lines or a tracing-log spawn error; the exit-0 shape relies on the bridge's zero-findings heuristic instead. Both are free-text heuristics tied to Codex's current wording.
